text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Police swooped in on five states early this month, arresting two drug kingpins who doubled as discotheque owners in the Kuala Lumpur area.

-- Sukom 98 Bhd executive chairman Hashim Mohamed Ali has dismissed the nition that his powers have eroded under the new organisational format for the 1998 Commonwealth Games now supervised by Youth and Sports Minister Muhyiddin Yassin.
-- About 40 percent of medicines sold in the country are imitation, Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob said on Thursday.
-- People who have lost money arising from certain banking services and have small claims of up to 25,000 ringgit can now resolve their complaints through the new Banking Mediation Bureau.
-- Saeaga Airlines will be spending some $600 million to buy 15 new wide-bodied Airbus 320 aircraft in the next 2-1/2 years, its executive chairman Ting Pek Khiing said.
-- The ringgit is not expected to weaken much in the wake of the latest round of crisis in Thailand which saw the baht reeling to a 12-year low, according to Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

-- The United Malays National Organisation headquarters will conduct its own investigation into the allegation that certain leaders and members of the Kemaman UMNO division went on a company-sponsored tour to Europe last month.
